source.body_text: In the 9th century, Baghdad had cheques, bills of exchange, international money transfers, and venture capital, all without interest. Explore how Caliph Harun al-Rashid built the world's first multicultural economic hub, how Abu Yusuf revolutionized tax policy, and how the hawala system moved money across continents on trust alone.

x.single_post: In 9th century Baghdad, a merchant could cash a cheque 4,000 miles away in Canton. The hawala system moved money across continents on handshakes — no banks required.
thread: In 9th century Baghdad, a merchant could cash a cheque 4,000 miles away in Canton. The hawala system moved money across continents on handshakes — no banks required.
Caliph Harun al-Rashid built the world's first multicultural economic hub. Jews, Christians, Muslims, and Zoroastrians traded side by side in Baghdad's markets.
Abu Yusuf wrote the first systematic treatise on tax policy. He argued that governments should tax wealth, not poverty — revolutionary thinking in the 9th century.

They had venture capital, international transfers, and bills of exchange. All without charging interest. Baghdad proved commerce could flourish on different principles. https://islamiceconomics.github.io/podcast.html#ep-3

linkedin.post: In the 9th century, Baghdad operated the world's most sophisticated financial system — all without charging interest. Merchants could cash cheques 4,000 miles away through the hawala system, built entirely on trust and reputation. Caliph Harun al-Rashid created the first truly multicultural economic hub where people of all faiths traded together. Abu Yusuf wrote the first systematic treatise on tax policy, arguing governments should tax wealth, not poverty — revolutionary thinking for the 9th century. They had venture capital, international money transfers, and bills of exchange. Commerce flourished on principles we're only now rediscovering in our search for ethical finance. The House of Wisdom explores how Baghdad's golden age offers lessons for today's economy. https://islamiceconomics.github.io/podcast.html#ep-3
